subject: Deployment pathway clarification & data isolation checklist
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medisys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment pathway clarification & data isolation checklist

Hi Alice / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to see the clinical routing flow and the strict egress controls you need for PHI. As discussed, I want to clarify a few items so we can recommend the right deployment pathway (Hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem) and get a short decision checklist back to your procurement team. I attached a one-page checklist but summarized the key asks here so you have them in the thread.

Quick recap of what I heard today:
- Primary requirement: no customer data may leave the customer-owned network unless encrypted and logged (audit window = 2 years).
- Prefer logical separation, but will evaluate Private VPC if there are compliance gaps (SOC2 + local encryption control).
- KMS/HSM residency and BYOK are important decision factors.

Questions for you (short bullets — easy yes/no where possible):
1) Is persistent model training/retraining on your side planned in the pilot? (yes/no) — affects whether we need long-lived data persistence on your network.
2) For encryption keys: do you require KMS keys to be customer-managed (BYOK) and housed in your cloud tenant?
3) Any regulatory constraints requiring physical air-gapped on-premise processing (true/false)?
4) Audit evidence: will the 3rd-party audit copies need to show token-level request traces or is session-level sufficient?

What Redwood can offer immediately:
- Hosted API with strict routing rules and configurable prefix caching (fastest to deploy).
- Redwood Dedicated: dedicated GPU pools in our cloud region with network egress restricted and enhanced logging. We can support customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest and provide token-level traces on request.
- Private VPC (managed control plane): we can package a private control plane in your VPC or an on-prem appliance for fully customer-hosted data processing.

Next steps I propose:
- You answer the bullets above (1–4) so we can produce a short matrix comparing tradeoffs and an ops/effort estimate.
- If Private VPC is required, we will schedule a 90-min security workshop with our infra team to scope KMS, HSM, and network routing.

Attachment: redwood_deployment_isolation_checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)

Thanks — will follow up with Grace (cc) on the technical specifics once we have your answers.

Best,
Markus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0168

From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medisys.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@medisys.com>, procurements@medisys.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment pathway clarification & data isolation checklist

Markus —

Thanks for the recap and checklist. Quick answers inline below: solid format.

1) Persistent training: no, not for the pilot. We're only running inference on inbound documents.
2) KMS: yes, BYOK required. Keys must be in our AWS account (us-east-1) and we need KMIP/HSM-backed keys for DR and compliance.
3) Air-gapped on-prem: false. We do not need an air-gapped environment for the pilot, but production may require stricter controls down the line.
4) Audit evidence: token-level traces preferred. Our audit team wants request/response fingerprints tied to user IDs.

Additional notes: procurement asked whether Redwood Dedicated supports a customer-managed control plane or whether that is only in Private VPC. Also, can you confirm whether Dedicated can be configured to restrict egress entirely (no data exfil) with logs forwarded to our S3?

Happy to jump on a follow-up call next week if needed — Rajiv and I are available Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Regards,
Alice Monroe
VP Security & Risk, MediSys Health
alice.monroe@medisys.com | +1 (212) 555-0222

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medisys.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment pathway clarification & data isolation checklist

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick answers, very helpful.

Short answers to procurement/security asks:
- Redwood Dedicated: network egress can be locked down via VPC peering and customer-controlled routing; we can enforce a deny-by-default egress policy and ship logs to an S3 bucket in your account using an IAM role you provision. That provides the strong egress guarantees you described.
- Customer-managed KMS: supported for both Dedicated and Private VPC. For Dedicated we require a cross-account role so Redwood can perform instance-level encryption ops; keys remain in your account and are BYOK/HSM-backed.
- Control plane residency: Redwood Dedicated has a managed control plane (hosted) - control plane metadata remains in Redwood (we offer contractual guarantees and audit logs). Private VPC gives you the option for a private control plane (we package a deployable control plane component for your VPC).

Operational impacts / tradeoffs (very high level):
- Dedicated: fastest to stand up for pilot, lower operational burden for MediSys, allows strict egress and BYOK. You will still rely on Redwood for control plane operations and patching.
- Private VPC: highest isolation, you get full control (control plane & data plane options), but requires more infra work and we recommend a 4–6 week delivery window for the pilot packaging + security validation.

Suggested next step: 60–90 min security workshop where we map the following: key residency model, S3 log flow, network routes, and sample audit evidence (token-level trace sample). Ben, can you add an ops-level estimate and available engineers for that workshop?

Attachment: pilot-scope-statement.pdf (pdf, 96 KB)

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Alice / Rajiv / Procurement team —

Great — thanks for confirming. Based on your answers we recommend the following for the pilot:

Recommendation (pilot): Redwood Dedicated with BYOK (KMS in your AWS account) and deny-by-default egress rules forwarding logs to your S3 bucket. Rationale: lowest friction to start (no control-plane install), supports HSM-backed keys, and provides the token-level traceability you requested.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Procurement: please confirm a short-form SOW approval window (we can provide a draft SOW for Dedicated pilot with the KMS and logging clauses).
- MediSys infra: create an S3 bucket and a cross-account IAM role for log delivery; share the role ARN and preferred region (us-east-1).
- Security: schedule the 90-min workshop (proposed times Tue/Wed 14:00–16:00 PST). Reply with availability and we will send calendar invites.

I've attached the checklist and scope statement for your records. If procurement requires a Private VPC option in parallel, we can surface a parallel estimate but that will add ~4–6 weeks to the timeline.

Attachments: redwood_deployment_isolation_checklist.xlsx, pilot-scope-statement.pdf

Thanks and happy to coordinate the calendar once procurement confirms.

Best,
Markus
